heroCommands.comment: Turn a website into a desktop app

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Pake turns any website into a lightweight desktop app for macOS, Windows or Linux with one command. It uses Rust and Tauri with the system's own web view, so the apps are small and don't bundle a browser.
sixtySeconds.problem: Web apps you use all day live in browser tabs, and Electron wrappers are large. The README says Pake installers are typically under 10 MB, nearly 20 times smaller than Electron packages.
whoFor: People who want web apps like ChatGPT or Notion as desktop apps
Developers packaging a web tool for desktop
AI agents packaging pages via the --json mode
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for tiny, fast desktop wrappers around websites. Beginners can download ready-made apps or use the Pake desktop app from pake.run instead of the command line.
requirements: Node.js and pnpm for the CLI

overview: The Pake CLI packages a URL into a desktop app. It fetches the website's icon automatically, and options let you set a custom icon, window size and a hidden title bar. The first build sets up the environment and takes a while; later builds are fast.

The repository also offers ready-made apps for sites like ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, YouTube, Notion and Excalidraw on its Releases page, and online building through GitHub Actions if you'd rather skip the command line. Apps support keyboard shortcuts, immersive windows, drag and drop, style customisation and ad removal.

For scripts and AI agents, pass --json for machine-readable output or describe apps with --config app.json. Pake is GPL-3.0 with an output exception, and apps you build are yours to use and distribute.
